kpi_framework.description: Structured KPI hierarchy organized by business domain. These KPIs define what creators should measure and optimize. Each KPI has a clear definition, computation, and relevance to creator business health.

kpis.name: publish_frequency
kpis.definition: Number of content items published per week
kpis.importance: consistency signal to algorithm and audience

kpis.name: cross_post_reach_multiplier

kpis.name: engagement_rate

kpis.target: varies by content type; > 3% is healthy

kpis.name: content_to_commerce_rate

kpis.importance: measures content as a revenue driver

kpis.name: average_watch_time

kpis.name: monthly_active_rate

kpis.name: member_churn_rate

kpis.name: contributor_ratio
kpis.definition: Members who posted or commented / total members * 100

kpis.name: time_to_first_post
kpis.definition: Hours between member join and their first post

kpis.name: creator_response_rate
kpis.definition: Member posts that received a creator reply / total member posts * 100

consumer_feed_algorithm.description: The algorithm that powers the Consumer Feed (Module 5) — determines what content consumers see, in what order. This directly impacts creator analytics because it determines content distribution.
consumer_feed_algorithm.implementation_note: Consumer Feed page exists but uses simple chronological ordering. No algorithmic ranking implemented.

factors.description: Signals that influence content ranking in the consumer feed

signals.name: recency
signals.description: Newer content ranks higher, with time decay function

signals.name: engagement_velocity
signals.description: Content gaining engagement quickly gets boosted (trending signal)

signals.name: creator_follow_status
signals.description: Content from followed creators ranks significantly higher

signals.name: content_type_affinity
signals.description: User's historical preference for content types (video vs text vs image)

signals.name: topic_relevance
signals.description: Content topic matches user's demonstrated interests

signals.name: engagement_rate
signals.description: Content's overall engagement rate as quality signal

signals.name: completion_rate
signals.description: For video/courses: what percentage of viewers finish

signals.name: creator_tier
signals.description: Pro/Business creators may get slight boost (premium feature)

signals.name: diversity_penalty
signals.description: Prevent feed from being dominated by single creator or content type

ranking.description: How signals combine into a final ranking score
ranking.formula_concept: score = recency_decay(age) * (w1*engagement_velocity + w2*follow_boost + w3*affinity + w4*relevance + w5*quality) - diversity_penalty
ranking.implementation_approach: Start with simple weighted linear model. Iterate to ML model when sufficient engagement data exists.
ranking.fallback: Chronological ordering when insufficient data for personalization (new users, cold start)

personalization.description: How the feed personalizes for individual consumers
personalization.cold_start: New users see trending content + editorial picks until sufficient engagement history (minimum 20 interactions)
personalization.warm_user: Personalized feed based on follow graph, engagement history, and content type preferences
personalization.explore_vs_exploit: 80% personalized (exploit) / 20% discovery (explore) to prevent filter bubbles
personalization.refresh_rate: Feed recalculates on pull-to-refresh or every 5 minutes of active browsing

design_constraints.description: Dashboard design constraints inherited from CreatorOS design identity
principles: Data-dense without clutter — every pixel earns its place
Monochrome primary with accent color for alerts and CTAs
Tables over cards for data-heavy views (content list, order history)
Sparklines inline with metrics for instant trend visibility
No glassmorphism, no gradients, no decorative elements
Mobile-first responsive — dashboard must work on phone
Loading states: skeleton screens, never spinners
Empty states: actionable guidance, not just 'no data'

color_semantics.accent: brand primary (TBD — see design identity canon)

chart_library.description: Chart library selection needed. Candidates: Recharts (React-native, lightweight), Chart.js (canvas-based, performant), D3 (maximum flexibility, highest complexity).
chart_library.recommendation: Recharts — best fit for React + TypeScript stack, good defaults, minimal config

open_questions.question: Should creators be able to build custom dashboards with drag-and-drop widget arrangement?
open_questions.context: Custom dashboards add significant implementation complexity (widget registry, layout persistence, permission scoping). Most creator platforms ship fixed dashboards first.
open_questions.recommendation: Ship fixed dashboard layout for v1. Add custom dashboards in v2 based on creator feedback.
open_questions.impact: HIGH — affects dashboard architecture, component design, and persistence layer

open_questions.question: Should there be a public API for creators to query their own analytics programmatically?
open_questions.context: API analytics access enables power creators to build custom reports, integrate with external tools (Notion, spreadsheets), and automate reporting. Adds API design and rate-limiting scope.
open_questions.recommendation: Expose read-only analytics API for Business and Enterprise tiers. Rate-limit at 100 requests/hour.
open_questions.impact: MEDIUM — requires API design, auth scoping by tier, rate limiting, documentation

open_questions.question: Should the platform provide benchmark data so creators can compare their metrics against platform averages?
open_questions.context: Benchmarks are valuable for creators to contextualize their performance (e.g., 'your engagement rate is in the top 20% of creators in your niche'). Requires computing and updating platform-wide aggregates, and deciding granularity (by niche, by tier, by product type).
open_questions.recommendation: Yes, for Pro tier and above. Compute weekly aggregates by product type and creator tier. Show percentile rankings.
open_questions.impact: MEDIUM — requires aggregate computation pipeline, privacy considerations, UI for comparisons

open_questions.question: What attribution model should be used for content-to-commerce conversion tracking?
open_questions.context: When a consumer views content and later purchases a product, how is that attributed? Options: last-touch (simplest), first-touch, linear (split credit), time-decay. Affects content_to_commerce_rate KPI accuracy.
open_questions.recommendation: Start with last-touch attribution (30-day window). Simplest to implement and explain to creators. Add multi-touch attribution as a Business tier feature later.
open_questions.impact: MEDIUM — affects all commerce analytics accuracy and creator decision-making

open_questions.question: Should AI-powered insights be surfaced on the dashboard (e.g., 'your engagement drops on Tuesdays' or 'this product converts 3x better with video content')?
open_questions.context: AI insights differentiate from commodity analytics tools. Aligns with UMH intelligence substrate. But adds LLM cost per creator per insight refresh cycle.
open_questions.recommendation: Yes, as a Pro tier feature. Generate weekly insights batch via UMH substrate. Display as 'AI Insights' card on dashboard. Start with 3 insight types: best posting time, top converting content format, churn risk alert.
open_questions.impact: HIGH — differentiating feature, requires UMH integration, LLM cost per creator
